title: Humour and teasing
job: Banter, irony, and when not to
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: presente, L1-M6's, which is where a tease is delivered
imperfetto, L2-M10's, in one lexicalised repair: scherzavo
passato prossimo, L2-M10's, in abbiamo riso and nowhere else
imperativo negativo, L4-M1's non plus infinitive, in non ti offendere

rules.text: THE EVALUATIVE SUFFIX MOVES THE TONE, NOT THE SIZE. -ino and -etto add warmth (attimino, poverino, bellino), -one adds size and fondness together (bacione), -accio adds contempt (tempaccio, parolaccia). This is the machinery Italian uses to say how it feels about a thing while naming it, and it is why an Italian sentence can be affectionate with no adjective in it at all. Read -ino as little and you will use it to mean small, which is the one thing it does not reliably mean.

THE PARTICLES OF MOCK PROTEST CARRY THE JOKE, BECAUSE NOTHING ELSE CAN. ma dai, ma va, addirittura, senti chi parla: short fixed noises that mark what follows, or what preceded, as not seriously meant. In speech the tone would do this work; this course has no audio at all, so the WORDS have to do it, and an item that is not funny on the page is not funny. Learn them as whole units — ma dai is not ma plus dai — and learn which direction each one pushes.

ENGLISH TEASES BY UNDERSTATEMENT AND ITALIAN BY EXAGGERATION. That is not a nuance, it is the whole difference: addirittura, esagerato, roba da matti. An English speaker who says it was quite good where an Italian says sei esagerato has not made a small stylistic slip, they have simply not been heard as joking. Overshoot on purpose, and expect to be overshot at.

THE REPAIR THAT CLOSES A TEASE IS AN IMPERFETTO. scherzavo, I was joking — never ho scherzato. The passato prossimo is perfectly grammatical and lands as a confession to a finished act, which turns a light tease into an apology for having committed one. This is a tense choice worth memorising as a lexeme rather than derived: one form, one job, and the alternative is not a weaker version of it.

THE ECHO REPLIES AND THE WORDS FOR THE JOKE ITSELF. anch'io answers a positive and neanch'io answers a negative, and they are single words with the elision inside them — anch'io is not anche plus io on the page. Around them: che ridere for what a laugh, buffo for funny in a way you smile AT, divertente for funny with no edge in it, esagerato for over the top, permaloso for touchy, and senza offesa and non ti offendere for the two ways of taking the edge off after the fact.

THE ALTERED WORDS ARE LEXICALISED, NOT PRODUCTIVE. The eight or so shown here are words a dictionary lists: carino, bellino, poverino, attimino, bacione, tempaccio, parolaccia. A learner who invents a ninth by rule is inventing a word, and it will be heard as one. Each altered word also keeps the gender of its base — parola is feminine, so it is parolaccia and never parolaccio — and the base itself stays where its own module put it.

sentences.cue: Oh come on, I don't believe it!

words.note: One protest spelled with two words. Neither half is doing its own job: nobody is being told to give anything, and the ma is not contrasting with anything.

sentences.trap: It is not the imperative of dare with ma in front of it. Splitting the pair gives dai, come on, plus an ordinary but — which is not the same move at all.
sentences.sound: ma DYE. dai rhymes with the English dye and takes the whole stress; ma is swallowed in front of it.

variations.changed: said alone, which is most of the time

variations.cue: Come off it, that's not true!
variations.changed: the disbelief said out loud after the particle

variations.cue: Oh come on, what a laugh!
variations.changed: che ridere after it, so the protest is friendly

mistake.why: Split apart, the two words go back to meaning what they say. The protest is the pair, in that order, with nothing between them.

sentences.usage: Reacting to news you find hard to believe, or to a friend who is laying it on thick.
sentences.mnemonic: Two small words, one raised eyebrow.

sentences.display: Ma va! Addirittura, non ci credo
sentences.cue: Get away! Really — I don't believe it
sentences.literal: But goes! Even-so, not there I-believe

words.note: Flatter disbelief than ma dai. The verb is va, the third person, and it is not aimed at anybody: the pair is one fixed noise.
Even, to that extent. Said alone it is a whole reaction — you did THAT? — and it is the exaggeration this kind of joking runs on.

sentences.trap: ma dai and ma va are not interchangeable. ma dai invites the other person to go on; ma va tells them to stop.
sentences.sound: ma VA. ad-dee-reet-TOO-ra: five syllables, a double d and a double t, both of them held.

variations.changed: alone, which is its usual size
the second half alone, as a whole answer
the denial spelled out after it

mistake.why: The form is va and not the vai you say to a friend. Nobody is being told to go anywhere, so the verb never agrees with anyone.

sentences.usage: Answering a claim you think is over the top, from a friend and never from a stranger.
sentences.mnemonic: ma dai pulls the story out; ma va pushes it away.

sentences.cue: I'm teasing you — I was joking

words.note: Tease, take the mickey. The person goes in front of the verb — ti prendo in giro — and giro is not doing any work you could look up.
The infinitive, and the shape a dictionary lists. It is not unkind in itself: what makes a tease cruel is who it is aimed at, not this verb.
The repair, and it is an imperfetto on purpose. ho scherzato is grammatical and lands as a confession to a finished act, not as a light correction.

sentences.trap: English also says I WAS joking, so the tense feels familiar — but the alternative is the trap: ho scherzato reads as an apology for something you did, which is exactly the weight a tease must not have.
sentences.sound: tee PREN-do een JEE-ro, sker-TSA-vo. The g of giro is soft, like the j of jeep; the z of scherzavo is a ts.

variations.changed: the repair alone, which is how it usually arrives
the tease without the repair behind it
prendi, and the question turned round on you

mistake.display: Ti prendo in giro, ho scherzato
mistake.why: ho scherzato closes the joke as a completed event and sounds like owning up to it. The repair is scherzavo, and only scherzavo.

sentences.usage: Said straight after a tease, to make sure it landed as one.
sentences.mnemonic: Walk them round in a circle, then say you were joking.

sentences.display: Senti chi parla! Non ti offendere
sentences.cue: Look who's talking! Don't take it the wrong way
sentences.literal: Hear who speaks! Not yourself offend

words.note: The comeback that turns a tease back on the teaser. Three ordinary words, frozen: the senti is not an order to listen to anything.
L4-M1's non plus an infinitive, with ti attached. It comes AFTER the tease and is what keeps one from turning into an insult.

sentences.trap: English hears listen at the front and waits for an instruction. Nothing is being asked here: the three words are one retort and the fourth word never comes.
sentences.sound: SEN-tee kee PAR-la. chi is kee and never chee; the stress sits on SEN and on PAR.

variations.changed: the comeback alone
the repair alone, with no tease in front
senza offesa added, so the comeback is softened as it lands

mistake.why: The frozen word is senti. ascolta is the ordinary verb for listen and turns a comeback into a plain instruction to pay attention.

sentences.usage: Turning a tease back on the person who made it, between people who know each other well.

sentences.display: Che tempaccio! Ho detto una parolaccia
sentences.cue: What foul weather! I've just sworn
sentences.literal: What weather-bad! I-have said a word-bad

words.note: tempo is L3-M4's and stays there. The -accio adds contempt and only contempt: this is not more weather, it is worse weather.
Built on parola with the same suffix, feminine because parola is. It is the name for the category; this module goes no further into it than that.

sentences.trap: -accio is not a size. tempaccio is not a lot of weather and parolaccia is not a long word: the ending carries disgust, and disgust is all it carries.
sentences.sound: ke tem-PAT-cho, pa-ro-LAT-cha. A double c before i or e is a held ch sound, and the i after it is silent.

variations.changed: oggi added, so the complaint gets a day
the second noun alone, as an exclamation
L4-M1's negative order in front of it

mistake.why: The suffix takes the gender of the word it lands on. parola is feminine, so it is parolaccia; parolaccio is a word Italian does not have.

sentences.usage: Complaining about the weather, or about what somebody has just said.

sentences.cue: Just a sec — I'm coming right away

words.note: attimo is L2-M7's. The -ino does not make the moment shorter, it makes the asking softer, and Italians tease each other about how often it is said.

sentences.trap: un attimino is not a smaller attimo. A learner who reads -ino as little will start using it to mean small and be heard as coy.
sentences.sound: oon at-tee-MEE-no. The double t is held; the stress falls on MEE and nowhere else.

variations.changed: alone, which is how it is usually heard
subito dropped, and the promise gets vaguer

variations.cue: I'm coming right away, one sec
variations.changed: the two halves swapped round

mistake.why: attimo is masculine and stays masculine when the ending changes. The article is un, and no suffix ever moves a word's gender.

sentences.usage: Asking somebody to wait — at a counter, on the phone, at a door.
sentences.mnemonic: -ino softens the ask; it does not shorten the wait.

sentences.display: Che carino! Che bellino! Un bacione, poverino!
sentences.cue: How sweet! How cute! A big kiss, poor thing!
sentences.literal: What dear-little! What beautiful-little! A kiss-big, poor-little!

words.note: Built on caro, dear, and drifted away from it: carino is light praise for a person, a thing or a gesture, with no weight behind it.
bello is L2-M3's and stays there. bellino is smaller PRAISE, not smaller beauty, and it is faintly patronising when said of an adult.
-one carries size and fondness at once. The plural bacioni is how a message to a friend signs off, where English would write love.
Sympathy, and between friends usually mock sympathy. Which one it is depends entirely on who is saying it about what, never on the word.

sentences.trap: None of these four is about size. -ino and -one move warmth, so a learner who hears bacione as a physically large kiss has read the wrong dimension entirely.
sentences.sound: ka-REE-no, bel-LEE-no, ba-CHO-ne, po-ve-REE-no. The ci of bacione is a cho sound, with the i silent.

variations.changed: one altered word alone
the sign-off on its own
both endings feminine, agreeing with the same person

mistake.why: The endings have to agree with the same person. carina and poverina go together, or carino and poverino; mixing them inside one breath is the giveaway.

sentences.usage: Cooing over a child, a photo or a small kindness — and, between friends, over a small misfortune.
sentences.mnemonic: -ino is a pat on the arm, -one is a hug.

sentences.display: Che ridere! Abbiamo riso, sei buffo
sentences.cue: What a laugh! We laughed — you're funny
sentences.literal: What to-laugh! We-have laughed, you-are funny

words.note: che plus a bare infinitive is a whole exclamation in Italian, where English needs a noun: not what a laughing, but what a laugh.
Taught as a pair on purpose. The bare participle riso is already L1-M8's rice, so a tap on that word alone opens a note about shopping.
Funny in a way you smile AT rather than with. divertente is the word with no edge in it, and the difference between them is the whole tease.

sentences.trap: riso is rice and the participle of ridere, spelled identically. Say abbiamo riso, ho riso, hai riso — and never leave the participle standing on its own.
sentences.sound: ke REE-de-re, ab-BYA-mo REE-zo, say BOOF-fo. The s of riso is a z sound; buffo has a double f and it is held.

variations.changed: the exclamation alone
tutta la sera added, so the laughing gets a length
molto in front, and the tease is aimed

mistake.why: ridere is the infinitive and cannot follow abbiamo. The participle is riso, however much it looks like the rice from the shopping module.

sentences.usage: Said in the retelling, after something funny has actually happened.
sentences.mnemonic: riso is rice until abbiamo is standing in front of it.

sentences.display: Senza offesa, ma sei esagerato e permaloso
sentences.cue: No offence, but you're over the top and touchy
sentences.literal: Without offence, but you-are exaggerated and touchy

words.note: Said BEFORE the thing that might offend, where non ti offendere is said after it. Both are fixed and neither is an apology.
Half complaint and half compliment, because exaggeration is how this kind of joking is done. Said of a person, not of a thing.
The word for somebody who cannot take a tease. Calling a friend permaloso is itself a tease, which is why it belongs in this module.

sentences.trap: English teases by understating and Italian by overstating. A learner who softens this to sei un po' troppo has not been gentler, they have simply not been heard as joking.
sentences.sound: SEN-tsa of-FE-za, e-za-je-RA-to, per-ma-LO-zo. The z of senza is a ts; both s sounds between vowels are z.

variations.changed: the accusation alone
one adjective instead of two

variations.cue: You're not funny, you're over the top
variations.changed: the two words set against each other

mistake.display: Senza offesa, ma sei esagerato e permalosa
mistake.why: One person, one gender, twice. esagerato is masculine and permalosa feminine; a single sentence cannot hold both endings about the same person.

sentences.usage: Answering a friend who has told a story far bigger than the thing that happened.
sentences.mnemonic: senza offesa goes in front, non ti offendere goes behind.

sentences.display: Sei divertente. Anch'io! Non sono buffo. Neanch'io!
sentences.cue: You're funny. — Me too! I'm not comical. — Nor am I!
sentences.literal: You-are entertaining. Also-I! Not I-am comical. Neither-I!

words.note: The neutral word for funny, said of a person or an evening. It carries no edge at all, which is what separates it from buffo.
One word on the page, apostrophe and all, and it answers a POSITIVE. anche is L1-M10's and io is L2-M5's; this is neither of them.
The answer to a NEGATIVE, and the one English speakers get wrong: after non sono, me too is wrong and neanch'io is the only reply.

sentences.trap: English can answer a negative with me neither or me too and be understood either way. Italian cannot: anch'io after a non sentence is heard as agreeing with the opposite of what was said.
sentences.sound: dee-ver-TEN-te, an-KEE-o, ne-an-KEE-o. The ch is a k sound and the apostrophe is not a pause.

variations.changed: the positive reply alone
the negative reply alone
molto in front, and no reply after it

mistake.why: anch'io agrees with a positive. After a non sentence it says the opposite of what the speaker means, and neanch'io is the only reply that works.

sentences.usage: Agreeing with a friend, in the two directions a conversation can be going.
sentences.mnemonic: anch'io after a yes, neanch'io after a no.

comprehensionPool.cue: Come off it, I don't believe it!
One sec, I'm coming right away
What a laugh! You're very funny
I'm not touchy. — Nor am I!
